patterns.name: Strategy
patterns.intent: Define a family of interchangeable algorithms behind one interface so the client can switch between them without conditional logic.
use_cases: Several pricing, shipping, payment or export variants selected at runtime
A growing set of behavioural variants that keep being added
applicability: The same operation exists in three or more variants
New variants are expected to be added regularly
The variants share inputs and outputs
structural_indicators: An interface or abstract class with several implementations
A context class that holds the interface and delegates to it
Implementations injected or selected outside the context
code_smells: Long if/else or switch chains that select behaviour by a type or kind value
Duplicated methods across classes that differ only in the algorithm
benefits: Each variant lives in its own class and can be tested in isolation
New variants are added without editing the existing conditional
Removes the growing conditional from the client
drawbacks: Adds an interface and one class per variant
The selection logic still has to live somewhere (factory, configuration or DI)
Indirection makes the control flow harder to follow for small cases
avoid_when: There are only two stable variants
The conditional is short and rarely changes

steps: Extract the common operation into an interface
Move each conditional branch into its own implementation
Let the context receive the implementation (constructor, registry or factory)
Replace the conditional with a call on the interface

examples.code:
public interface IShippingCost { decimal Cost(Order order); }
public class Checkout { private readonly IShippingCost _shipping; public Checkout(IShippingCost shipping) => _shipping = shipping; }

confidence_notes: Strategy, State and Bridge share the same structure; the analyzer reports the structure, not the designer's intent
An interface with implementations alone is ordinary polymorphism; a delegating context is needed for a likely Strategy

existing.explanation: A context delegates to an abstraction that has several implementations.

opportunities.explanation: Behaviour is selected by a conditional chain with three or more cases.
Behaviour is selected by checking the runtime type.
Classes expose the same operations without a shared abstraction.

patterns.name: Observer
patterns.intent: Let any number of dependents react to a state change of a subject without the subject knowing their concrete types.
use_cases: Several components must react when an order, document or setting changes
UI updates, notifications, audit logging or cache invalidation triggered by one event
applicability: The set of reacting components changes over time
The subject should not depend on the reacting components
structural_indicators: A collection of listeners with registration methods
A notification loop calling the same method on every listener
code_smells: A method that calls the same update method on several hard-coded collaborators
Notification code duplicated in every place that changes the state
benefits: New reactions are added without changing the subject
Subject and observers are loosely coupled
drawbacks: Notification order and error handling become implicit
Event chains are harder to debug
avoid_when: There is exactly one fixed reaction
The reactions must run in a strict, documented order with shared transactions

steps: Define an observer interface with the notification method
Give the subject a list of observers and registration methods
Replace direct calls with a loop over the observers
Register the existing reactions as observers at the wiring point

confidence_notes: A loop over a collection that calls a method is also ordinary batch processing; registration of received objects is required for a confirmed Observer
Language events (C# event declared and raised) are strong evidence

existing.explanation: Received objects are stored in a collection and notified in a loop.
The class declares and raises an event.

opportunities.explanation: The same method is called on several hard-coded collaborators.

patterns.name: Factory Method
patterns.intent: Move object creation behind a method that returns an abstraction, so clients do not depend on concrete classes.
use_cases: Choosing a concrete implementation from configuration or input
Centralising construction that is repeated across the code base
applicability: Clients create concrete classes that share an abstraction
The same construction logic is repeated in several places
Subclasses must decide which concrete product to create
structural_indicators: A method whose declared return type is an abstraction and which creates concrete classes
An abstract or virtual creation method overridden in subclasses
code_smells: The same concrete class instantiated in many places
benefits: Clients depend on the abstraction only
One place to change when a new concrete class is added
drawbacks: Adds a creator method or class
Can hide simple constructor calls behind indirection
avoid_when: Only one concrete class exists and no other is planned
A dependency-injection container already performs the selection

steps: Make sure the products share an abstraction
Move the construction (including the selection) into a creator method returning the abstraction
Replace scattered constructor calls with calls to the creator

examples.code: public static IExporter Create(string format) => format switch { "csv" => new CsvExporter(), "pdf" => new PdfExporter(), _ => throw new NotSupportedException(format) };

confidence_notes: A static method with a switch over types is a Simple Factory; the classic Factory Method requires an overridden creation method
Python constructors are recognised by capitalised call names, which is a heuristic

existing.explanation: An abstract or virtual creation method returning an abstraction is overridden by subclasses.
A method declared to return an abstraction creates concrete implementations.

opportunities.explanation: Conditional branches create different concrete classes.
The same concrete class is constructed in many places.

patterns.name: Adapter
patterns.intent: Make an existing class with an incompatible interface usable through the interface the client expects.
use_cases: Integrating a third-party SDK or a legacy API behind an existing abstraction
Replacing a subsystem without changing its clients
applicability: An abstraction already exists for the role the new component should play
The new component cannot be changed to implement it
structural_indicators: A class implements the target interface and delegates to a differently shaped adaptee
code_smells: Client code converting data and calling a foreign API directly in many places
Conditionals that branch on which external system is used
benefits: Clients keep using the existing abstraction
The foreign or legacy API is isolated in one class
drawbacks: Adds a translation layer that must be kept in sync with both interfaces
Large interface mismatches lead to complicated adapters
avoid_when: The new component can implement the target interface directly
No abstraction exists yet and only one implementation is planned

steps: Identify the existing target interface
Create an adapter class that implements it
Hold the adaptee in the adapter and translate each call
Register the adapter where the other implementations are wired

confidence_notes: Delegation through a field is also used by Decorator and Proxy; the adaptee must not implement the target interface
Adapter opportunities are driven by the requested change: the code alone rarely shows an incompatible interface
Only adaptees that are not defined in the indexed repository (external SDKs and libraries) are reported, because services delegating to their own repositories look structurally identical

existing.explanation: A class implements an interface by delegating to a collaborator of another type.

opportunities.explanation: An abstraction with several implementations exists, so a new external component can be adapted to it.

patterns.name: Facade
patterns.intent: Offer one simple entry point to a group of collaborating subsystem classes.
use_cases: Clients repeat the same sequence of calls to several subsystem components
Hiding a legacy subsystem behind a smaller API
applicability: Several clients use the same subset of a subsystem in the same way
Clients do not need the full power of the subsystem
structural_indicators: A class whose methods mostly delegate to three or more collaborator types
code_smells: The same call sequence repeated across callers
Functions that reach into many files of one subsystem
benefits: Clients depend on one class instead of many
The subsystem can change behind a stable entry point
drawbacks: A facade can grow into a god class
Adds a layer that may duplicate subsystem APIs
avoid_when: Only one client uses the subsystem
Clients need fine-grained control over the subsystem

steps: Identify the repeated call sequence
Create a facade method that performs it
Move the clients to the facade one by one

confidence_notes: Service classes and controllers often delegate to many collaborators; whether they are intended facades cannot be decided structurally

existing.explanation: A class mostly forwards calls to several collaborator types.

opportunities.explanation: Several clients call the same group of subsystem functions.

patterns.name: Decorator
patterns.intent: Add optional responsibilities to an object by wrapping it in objects that implement the same interface.
use_cases: Logging, caching, retry, authorisation or metrics around an existing service
Combinable optional features that would otherwise need many subclasses
applicability: The behaviour to add is orthogonal to the core logic
Several optional behaviours must be combinable
structural_indicators: A class implements an interface and wraps another instance of that interface
code_smells: Subclasses that only add behaviour before or after calling the base implementation
Cross-cutting code duplicated in many methods
benefits: Behaviour is added without modifying the wrapped class
Decorators can be combined in different orders
drawbacks: Object identity and wrapping order become important
avoid_when: The service has no interface and introducing one is costly
A framework mechanism (middleware, interceptors, Python decorators) already covers the concern

steps: Make sure the service is used through an interface
Create a decorator that implements the interface and holds the wrapped instance
Forward each call and add the extra behaviour
Wrap the service where it is created or registered

examples.code: public class LoggingPaymentService : IPaymentService { private readonly IPaymentService _inner; public LoggingPaymentService(IPaymentService inner) => _inner = inner; public Task Pay(Order o) { _log.Info(o.Id); return _inner.Pay(o); } }

confidence_notes: Wrapping the same interface is also how Proxy and Composite are built

existing.explanation: A class implements an interface and forwards to a wrapped instance of the same interface.

opportunities.explanation: Subclasses add behaviour around the base implementation.

patterns.name: Repository
patterns.intent: Mediate between the domain and the persistence layer with a collection-like interface for aggregates.
use_cases: Hiding ORM or SQL access behind domain-oriented methods
Making business logic testable without a database
applicability: Business code queries the database directly in many places
The persistence technology should be replaceable or mockable
structural_indicators: A type with get/find/add/update/delete style operations
The type depends on a database or ORM API
code_smells: Business logic mixed with persistence calls
benefits: Persistence details live in one place
Domain logic can be tested with an in-memory implementation
drawbacks: Thin repositories over an ORM add little value
avoid_when: The ORM context is already used as a unit of work with few queries
The application is a thin CRUD layer

steps: Define an interface with the operations the domain needs
Move the persistence code into an implementation
Inject the interface into the services

examples.code: public interface IOrderRepository { Task<Order?> Find(int id); Task Add(Order order); }

confidence_notes: Operation names are only supporting evidence; a dependency on a persistence API is required
Supported reliably for C#, Java and Python code that uses recognisable ORM or database types

existing.explanation: A type offers collection-like operations and depends on a persistence API.
